description: Tracks adapter call frequency using an in-memory sliding window counter to prevent quota exhaustion and upstream API rate limit (429) errors before they occur. Compares the current calls-per-second or calls-per-minute against the adapter's contract limit from the catalog. If the limit is approached, the hook introduces a calculated delay rather than allowing the call to proceed and fail. Especially important for government APIs (GSTN, CIBIL) with strict TPS contracts and for Twilio and Razorpay which impose per-account rate limits that incur penalties.
use_cases: Preventing 429 rate limit errors on GSTN before they occur
Throttling CIBIL bureau calls to stay within TPS contract
Proactive delay injection for Twilio SMS bursts
Protecting Razorpay payment API quota in high-volume processing
Multi-tenant rate isolation to prevent one client from exhausting quota
when_to_use: Attach to all adapters with TPS or RPM rate limits — especially GSTN, CIBIL, Experian, Twilio, and Razorpay. Critical in high-volume batch or concurrent processing scenarios.
trigger_condition: Before the outbound network call is made to the adapter

input_parameters.description: Client making the call (for per-client rate tracking)
Current call count in the rate window
Maximum allowed calls per window from catalog contract

output.on_success: Call allowed; current_rate attached to request context
output.on_failure: Call delayed by calculated wait_ms; rate_limit_warning emitted

error_codes.HOOK_002: Throttling wait exceeded max pipeline drift.
error_codes.HOOK_003: Extreme quota overrun — blocking further requests.
